summary: Replace the plain grid with a DP over axis-aligned recursive layouts. Each region is split into a k×k grid, optionally with one m×m merged corner block, and each block or cell recursively holds its own best arrangement. This yields layouts such as 7/3 for n=6 and 2.5 for n=7, and it works for any n.

Extend the grid DP so a k×k grid can hold two merged square blocks, one in each of two opposite corners (m1+m2 ≤ k), each filled recursively with its best arrangement. This adds layouts that may beat the single-block ones for larger n; the single-block layouts are kept as a special case.

I reduced the leaf-square shrink factor from 1e-9 to 1e-10 and raised the cap on grid size in the DP from 12 to 14, so grid sizes are not limited for larger n. This is a small precision and coverage tweak, not a new layout family.
I lowered the leaf-square shrink from 1e-9 to 1e-11, so less of the total is lost to the safety margin. The DP layouts are unchanged, and the gain is tiny.
I raised the grid-size limit in the DP from sqrt(N)+2 to sqrt(N)+3, with a cap of 14, so slightly finer k×k grids are considered. The layout families are unchanged and the gain, if any, is small.
I raised the DP's grid-size cap from 12 to 16, so larger n are no longer limited to a 12×12 grid. The layout families are unchanged and runtime stays small.

I tightened the DP's tie-breaking tolerance from 1e-12 to 1e-14 so it no longer discards layouts that are slightly better by tiny margins. The layout families are unchanged, so any gain is expected to be very small.

I raised the DP's grid-size limit to sqrt(N)+4 with a cap of 16, so it considers finer k×k grids with merged corner blocks for larger n. The layout families are unchanged, so any gain is likely small.

I generalised the merged-corner-block layouts so a k×k grid can hold t equal m×m blocks (t up to (k//m)²), each filled recursively. The block counts and the remaining cell counts come from the same DP table, so this adds layout families beyond the single-block case.

I added a "pad" option to the DP: if the best layout for N-1 squares is at least as good as every layout found for N, use it and append a zero-side square. This guarantees the value never decreases as n grows, and the layout families are otherwise unchanged.

I generalised the merged-corner layout so a k×k grid can hold t equal m×m blocks (t up to (k//m)²) that share one fill count b. Each block is filled recursively, and the remaining cells use the same DP table. This adds layout families beyond the single-block case.

I added a second layout family to the DP: a k×k grid holding two merged square blocks of different sizes (m1 and m2, with m1+m2 ≤ k) in opposite corners.
